moat_against: ROIC proxy only ~4-12% over the last decade and negative in 2023 and 2025 (impairment years) — returns have not stayed well above the cost of capital
Industry-wide fee compression and the shift to low-cost passive; blended fee yield keeps eroding
Nasdaq-100 exclusivity ended — BlackRock's IQQ launched at a 10bp net fee against QQQ, chipping at the flagship franchise
Sub-scale vs BlackRock, Vanguard and State Street in ETF distribution and pricing power
AUM and revenue are market-beta driven: 5-yr revenue CAGR is only 0.7%; a drawdown cuts fees mechanically
Goodwill/intangibles-heavy balance sheet with recurring non-cash impairments (operating losses in 2023 and 2025)
moat_for: QQQ franchise: ~$498.9B AUM (Sep 2026), the 2nd-most-traded US ETF — liquidity and adviser-workflow network effects a cheaper rival cannot quickly replicate
Scale: $2.5T ending AUM (Q2 2026) with global distribution across Americas, EMEA and APAC
Product breadth beyond QQQ: ETF/index suite, fundamental fixed income and equities, private markets ($134.9B), China JV ($166.3B)
Flow momentum: 12 consecutive quarters of net long-term inflows; record $45.1B in Q2 2026, $67B in H1 (7% annualized organic growth)
Operating leverage at scale: adjusted operating margin 37.5% in Q2 2026, up from 31.2% a year earlier
moat_justification: A real but narrow franchise: QQQ's liquidity moat and $2.5T scale are genuine, but measured ROIC (roic_proxy ~4-12%, negative in the 2023 and 2025 impairment years) has never compounded well above the cost of capital, fees compress structurally, and BlackRock's IQQ ends the Nasdaq-100 exclusivity. Moderate moat, not strong.
name: Invesco Ltd.
one_liner: Decent-quality asset manager with a narrow QQQ/scale moat (5/10), but at $28.20 it does not clear the 15% hurdle on the normalized base — weighted IRR 11.3%, weighted IV@15% $19.61; it clears 15% only at ~$19.61 or below (method range C on the median base to B on the TTM base).
